newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks end lower on late profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks end lower on late profit-taking.

text.p: Taiwan share prices reversed early gains to end slightly lower on Thursday after profit-taking emerged in the final hour. Brokers said the market would consolidate around the strong 7,000-point barrier.
The index closed 24.15 points or 0.35 percent lower at 6,919.49. Turnover was a relatively modest T$79 billion.
Profit-taking was heaviest in electronics and plastics, which had enjoyed substantial gains while leading a wider market rise begun in mid-November.
"The market is a little overheated recently but the overall outlook remains good," said Allen Huang of National Securities.
Huang foreign fund entries were expected following news that Taiwan stock-index futures and options would be listed in January by exchanges in Singapore and Chicago.
"It is good news in the long run because taiwan is opening financial markets wider to foreign investors. But we can't expect foreign funds to come in at once," he said.

Financials outperformed the market to rise slightly on the futures news. Cathay Life, among the top 10 most actively traded issues, gained T$3 or 1.69 percent to T$180. Electronics saw profit-taking. Acer lost T$2 or 3.77 percent to T$51 and United Microelectronics lost T$1.4 or 3.36 percent T$40.3.
Nan Ya Plastics, a key member of Taiwan's influential Formosa group, lost T$1 or 1.45 percent to T$68 also on profit-taking after posting solid gains in previous days.
Brokers said they were still optimistic about blue chips and conglomerate issues, noting signs for a domestic economic recovery in the fourth quarter of 1997.
"It's only a problem of time that the index will climb above the 7,000-point barrier," said Joe Chiou of Taiwan Securities.
